blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Choosing the right supply chain model is less about following a textbook and more about matching the design to the reality of the product. A stable, high-volume product with predictable demand usually lives in a classic make-to-stock model. A custom, high-value product with variable demand needs make-to-order. Products in between need hybrids.

The cost of getting it wrong is not small. A company running make-to-stock on a custom product drowns in obsolete inventory. One running make-to-order on a commodity frustrates customers who expect fast delivery. Either mistake compounds over time until the mismatch becomes visible in the numbers.

The right question, before any investment, is simple: how predictable is demand for this product, and how much variety does the customer actually want? The honest answer usually points to the right model.

items.q: According to the text, which model suits a stable, high-volume product with predictable demand?
items.why: "A stable, high-volume product with predictable demand usually lives in a classic make-to-stock model."

items.q: What happens to a company that runs make-to-stock on a custom product?
options: It delivers faster than its rivals
items.why: "A company running make-to-stock on a custom product drowns in obsolete inventory."

items.q: What two questions does the text say you should ask before any investment?
options: How predictable is demand, and how much variety does the customer want?
How large is the factory, and how many staff do we need?
How strong is the brand, and how loyal are the customers?
How cheap is the product, and how fast can we ship it?
items.why: "how predictable is demand for this product, and how much variety does the customer actually want?"

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: A textbook rule should decide your supply chain model.
A mismatch eventually shows up in the numbers.
The best model depends on the nature of the product.
Products in between fit and stock may need a hybrid.
items.why: Inferência: o texto abre dizendo que a escolha é "less about following a textbook" — logo, o autor discordaria de deixar o livro-texto decidir.

items.q: The phrase "Either mistake compounds over time" suggests that…
options: the two mistakes cancel each other out
the mistakes are cheap to fix immediately
the damage grows and gets worse if left uncorrected
only one of the two models can ever fail
items.why: Inferência: "compounds" indica que o custo se acumula até ficar visível nos números — não é um erro que se resolve sozinho.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Harry ajudando o time do novo produto. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Okay, before we lock the factory layout, let's slow down for a second. The whole thing hinges on one question: how predictable is demand for this line, and how much variety will customers actually ask for?

Right now I'm hearing two very different products described as if they were one. If demand were stable and the spec were fixed, I'd say go make-to-stock — build ahead, fill the warehouse, ship the moment an order lands. But that's not what the sales forecast is telling us. The variety is high and the volumes swing month to month.

If we built to stock on a product this variable, we'd be sitting on obsolete inventory by the third quarter. And if we went pure make-to-order on the fast-moving version, we'd frustrate the customers who expect it off the shelf. So my honest recommendation is a hybrid: stock the stable, high-volume items and build the custom ones to order.

The point is, we decide this now. Changing the model after the layout is set is expensive and disruptive, and I'd rather we got it right before a single machine is bolted down.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does Harry want the team to settle BEFORE locking the factory layout?
options: How large the warehouse should be
How predictable demand is and how much variety customers want
items.why: "how predictable is demand for this line, and how much variety will customers actually ask for?"

items.q: According to Harry, when WOULD make-to-stock be the right call?
options: If the customer wanted maximum variety
If demand were stable and the spec were fixed
If the product were fully custom
items.why: "If demand were stable and the spec were fixed, I'd say go make-to-stock."

items.q: What does Harry finally recommend?
options: A hybrid: stock the stable items, build the custom ones to order
items.why: "a hybrid: stock the stable, high-volume items and build the custom ones to order."

items.q: Why does Harry say "we decide this now"?
options: Because the sales team is waiting for numbers
Because the customers have cancelled their orders
Because the warehouse is already full
Because changing the model after the layout is set is expensive and disruptive
items.why: Inferência: ele insiste em decidir antes porque "changing the model after the layout is set is expensive and disruptive."

items.q: What can you infer about the sales forecast Harry has seen?
options: It predicts falling demand across the board
It points to a single, stable product
It shows high variety and volumes that swing month to month
items.why: Inferência: ele diz que a previsão NÃO aponta para demanda estável — "The variety is high and the volumes swing month to month."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The plant was full of obsolete stock nobody would ever buy." Obsolete means…
options: out of date and no longer useful
items.why: Obsolete = obsoleto, fora de uso — estoque que perdeu valor e ninguém compra.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Because demand for this line is so ___, we cannot plan production a year ahead."
items.why: Variable = variável: oscila, então não dá para planejar com um ano de antecedência.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "A ___ between the model and the product eventually shows up in the numbers."
items.why: Mismatch = descompasso: o modelo não combina com o produto.

items.q: "Salt is a commodity: buyers expect it cheap and off the shelf." A commodity is…
items.why: Commodity = produto padronizado e intercambiável, comprado principalmente pelo preço.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "For the items in between, we run a ___ model — some to stock, some to order."
items.why: Hybrid = híbrido: combina os dois modelos para os produtos intermediários.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em decisões de cadeia de suprimentos. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Operations still has to sign off on the make-to-order plan." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We'll roll out the new model plant by plant." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "The logistics head pushed back on the make-to-stock forecast." She…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, questionar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "They agreed on the hybrid model but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Switching a few SKUs to order won't move the needle on inventory costs." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
